barclay_17860410.summary: Barclay reports from Madrid that Lamb's mission to Algiers has failed: no peace without a larger sum, and the Dey refuses to treat.
barclay_17860410.en: . no peace can be made until Congress grant a larger sum to pay for it , and that he will return to Spain to wait for orders s . tj_17870704.summary: Jefferson reports a conference on Barclay's arrest at Bordeaux with Montmorin's first secretary (Rayneval, by the editors' conjecture); the word the editors read as 'sea' is a group that means 'larg-' elsewhere in the code.
tj_17870704.en: Yesterday I had a long conference with M. de [Rayneval?]. It is impossible for a person to be more cordially disposed than M. de Montmorin but opposition from another quarter of the [495: larg-; the editors' "sea" is not supported] and the difficulty of the case [trouble?] him. [Rayneval?] observed to me that there was no country in Europe but France which took any notice of the character of a minister en passage between two other nations ... and ended by pressing the distress in which M. de Montmorin found himself, and how much they should be relieved by an amicable arrangement.

tj_17910411.summary: Jefferson urges Carmichael to work for a joint front against the British navigation act and for the free navigation of the Mississippi.
tj_17910411.en: That of a co-operation against the British navigation act and the Arrangement of our Affairs on the Missisippi . The former if it can be effected will form a remarkable and memorable Epoch in the History and freedom of the Ocean : Mr. Short will press it at Paris and Colo. Humphreys at Lisbon : the latter will shew most at first : and as to the latter be so good as to observe always that the Right of navigating the Missisippi is considered as so palpable that the Recovery of it will produce Sensation than that of a Gross Injustice removed .
